images.caption: Figure 1:DyCraftis an end-to-end agentic system for generating long-horizon animated 3D scenes from text prompts.Our system allows GPT-6-Astra coding agents to write minute-long 3D animations in Blender, depicting humanoid robots, human characters, and physical mechanisms. 3D moments from the authored films are shown above. Project page:https://dy-craft.github.io

Figure 2:Failure modes of bare agents.The top row shows GPT-6-Astra with Codex producing interpenetration, missing contact, grasp failure, motion discontinuity, unusable layout, and faked dynamics.
The bottom row shows corresponding results produced byDyCraftwith GPT-6-Astra.

Figure 3:Overview ofDyCrafton an example.A humanoid robot carries a wide panel through a narrow doorway. Following pose-to-pose animation,DyCraftbreaks authoring into steps that the agent can check individually. The sparse user prompt (1) is first expanded into detailed scene and motion briefs (2), which the agent uses to build the scene in CAD (3). The agent then plans key poses and object states as a 3D storyboard (4). After inspecting and verifying these states, the agent authors motion connecting them with domain-specific tools (5). Verifiers check every frame (6), catching errors in the storyboard states and motions: here, the arm passes through the torso (orange). The agent repeatedly revises the scene and motion before rendering the final film (7).

Figure 4:Scene authoring with CAD tools.Scene components authored byDyCraft(top) and by a bare agent
(bottom) for a marble run (both GPT-6-Astra). CAD operations allowDyCraftto construct
precise solid geometry, whereas the bare agent approximates the same components with primitives and thickened
surfaces that intersect or fail to connect.

Figure 5:Motion authoring tools.Motion authored byDyCraft(top) and by a bare agent (bottom) for the same
prompts. Using domain-specific techniques such as physical simulation and inverse kinematics,DyCraftproduces
motion that stays physically plausible, avoids interpenetration, and responds to dynamics.
The bare agent’s hand-scripted motion often violates these constraints.
Orange marks
bare-agent defects and blue arrows indicate time.

Figure 6:Verifiers.Each column shows a state that fails a verifier (top).
After agent repair, the verifier passes (bottom).
Verifiers for interpenetration, support, and joint limits catch errors that are
easily missed by visual inspection, such as characters passing through furniture,
objects floating above their supports, and joints that violate anatomical limits or rotate about a wrong axis.

Figure 7:Qualitative comparison with VIGA and a bare agent.Please view our video results on the supplemental webpage. Each column corresponds to an event described
in the prompt and shows the frame at which it occurs in each method’s animation; events that a
method does not produce are marked as not performed.
Compared withDyCraft, the bare agent produces simpler scenes with physically implausible motion and VIGA fails to generate several key events.
Translucent overlays show earlier poses, trails
indicate fast motion, and the main actor is highlighted in blue.
Figure 8:Ablation examples on barista making coffee.For each variant, we show defects overDyCrafton the same action.
